narrative: Ramp = the AI-native finance platform that gives 70,000 companies real-time visibility and automated control over every dollar of spend (auto-code 75%+, close books on time, catch waste before it hits margin). Enormous, sustained programs: 2,597 Google creatives (1,805 video, always-on since Jan 2022) + 1,389 LinkedIn creatives (image-heavy, deep vertical ABM — Healthcare/Consulting/Franchisors/Retail/Nonprofit/Immigration, named-account personalization). Mirror in Ramp's OWN language: Ramp closed the loop on spend for its customers — but its own growth engine runs the way finance ran before Ramp: spend out across channels, signups in-product, revenue in the CRM, nothing joined in real time. 'If you can't see it, you can't stop it' applies to their paid engine. Arc (light-first, 2 darks = statement + pilot): hero(plain)+agent-card → homework(white) → mirror statement(dark) → capabilities(white, numbered + outcome pills) → agentLoop(tint) → recommendations(white, rich agent cards) → comparison TABLE(tint) → defensibility(white) → integrations(white) → pilot(dark) → booking(white).

card.title: 1,389 LinkedIn creatives, 6 verticals — but 'Healthcare' and 'Consulting' convert to funded accounts at very different rates
card.found: Your vertical ABM runs the same play across Healthcare, Consulting, Franchisors, Retail and Nonprofit — but two of those verticals produce signups that reach a funded card, and the other three mostly stall at signup.
card.why: Budget is split evenly across verticals by volume, not by which vertical actually becomes a paying account — so spend is anchored to reach, not to revenue.
card.move: Shift budget toward the two verticals that fund accounts, hold the middle, and pause the vertical creatives with no funded account in 90 days.
card.impact: More funded accounts on the same spend

sections.heading: We studied how Ramp runs paid *before writing a word*.
sections.body: Pulled from your public Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, July 2026. It's one of the largest, most deliberate paid programs we've seen in software — two heavy channels running distinct jobs. Here's what we saw — and where an agent layer earns its keep.

channels.label: Always-on brand + performance video
channels.body: 'Never chase a receipt again,' 'Love closing the books — on time,' 'Smarter financial decisions,' 'Put automation where manual work used to live' — 1,805 video, 432 text and 360 image creatives, running continuously since January 2022. A four-and-a-half-year, always-on YouTube + search engine.

channels.label: AI-native, all-in-one — segmented to the account
channels.body: 'Cards, expenses, bill payments and banking — in the blink of AI,' 'Consolidate banking, cards & AP on Ramp,' 'auto-code 75%+ of transactions.' Deep vertical ABM — Healthcare, Consulting, Franchisors, Retail, Nonprofit, Immigration — with named-account personalization and competitor call-outs. Nearly every one carries copy. Your brand and account-acquisition engine.

sections.footer: Two heavy channels, 3,986 live creatives — one of the deepest software paid programs we've torn down. The gap isn't the ads — it's which of them actually becomes a funded account in Ramp, correlated across Google intent, every LinkedIn ABM touch, and product signup, and acted on daily. That's the layer Petavue owns.

sections.eyebrow: The one line of spend you can't see
sections.heading: You gave 70,000 finance teams real-time control of every dollar they spend. Which of your own 3,986 ads actually funds an account?
sections.body: Ramp exists so finance teams stop finding out where the money went at month-end. But your own growth engine runs the way finance ran before Ramp — spend across Google and LinkedIn, signups in the product, revenue in the CRM — and nothing joins them daily. 'If you can't see it, you can't stop it' is your line. Petavue closes that seam for your acquisition the way Ramp closed it for your customers' spend.

sections.heading: Point the agents at a goal. Agents run the rest.
sections.body: Set a goal in your own terms — cost-per-funded-account on Google, funded signups by vertical — and the agent works out what to watch and what to do, on your numbers.

goals.text: Cut cost-per-funded-account on Google 20% — without dropping signup volume.
goals.result: Agents watch all 2,597 creatives daily and move budget toward the terms and videos that produce funded accounts, not just signups.

goals.text: Get every high-fit vertical signup routed before it goes cold.
goals.result: Agents learn the path your funded accounts took, catch the ones that stall before first card spend, and hand them to sales or a nurture.

steps.title: Verify

sections.heading: Always know your next move.
sections.body: One engine watches paid-media efficiency; the other watches signups against your golden path. Two live examples, built for Ramp.

cards.title: Your top 40 always-on videos absorb most of the Google budget — but three of them haven't funded an account in 90 days
cards.found: A handful of your 1,805 videos have run continuously since 2022 and still take the largest share of spend, yet three of the highest-spend cuts haven't produced a funded account in the last quarter — signups, yes; funded cards, no.
cards.why: Budget is anchored to tenure and view volume, not to which creative actually becomes a paying account — the classic always-on drift.
cards.move: Rotate spend from the three zero-fund veterans into the two vertical cuts converting above blended, and cap frequency on the fatigued long-tail.

cards.title: 18 ICP accounts signed up from your Healthcare ABM, hit the ERP-sync step, and stalled — none routed
cards.found: Over 14 days, 18 companies matching your best funded-account profile signed up from the Healthcare vertical, reached the accounting/ERP-sync step, and went quiet before first card spend.
cards.why: This is the exact pattern before several of your recent sales-assisted funded accounts — high-fit companies stalling at the one step that predicts activation.
cards.move: Route the largest accounts to sales today as a named list, and enroll the rest in an activation nurture keyed to the ERP-sync step they stalled on.
